title: The Xcode project: targets, schemes, bundle id and Info.plist

videos.script: This course builds an iPhone app. A study planner, with the same screens and the same data as its Android and React Native twins. {{wall}} And the first thing it says is where the wall is. Xcode runs only on a Mac. So does SwiftUI, and so does the simulator. {{split}} But most of an app is not its screens. It is its data and its rules, and those are plain Swift. Swift runs on Linux. So every lesson puts that half in a Swift package, and you practise it on any computer. {{lab}} Today you install the toolchain, check its signature, and break it three ways on purpose. {{package}} Then you write the planner's core. Five files, one program that prints a week's total, and two tests. {{project}} Then the other half. What an Xcode project is made of: targets, schemes, a bundle identifier that can never change, {{plist}} and Info.plist, the file an app uses to describe itself. You read one with a few lines of Swift, and catch two mistakes in it. Where something needs a Mac, the lesson says so, every time.
